questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most suitable word.

At that time, I only knew that I adored the way he laughed for no ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'** i.e. **'Reason'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** most suitable word** to fill in the blank is **"reason".**
 
• The reason why this answer is correct is that the phrase **"laughed for no reason" **is a common English expression that means someone is laughing without any obvious cause or stimulus.
 
• It's **typically used to** describe a spontaneous or uncontrollable expression of joy or amusement.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* At that time, I only knew that I adored the way he laughed for no **reason**.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's briefly examine the other options:
 
 
• **"Just" -** This word doesn't fit the context of the sentence. "Just" is an adverb that means 'very recently' or 'exactly', and it doesn't make sense to laugh for no 'just'.
 
• **"Disbelief" -** This word also doesn't fit the context. "Disbelief" is a noun that means a refusal or inability to accept that something is true or real, and it doesn't make sense to laugh for no 'disbelief'.
 
• **"Account" -** This option doesn't fit the context either. In the given context, 'account' would imply a record or report of financial income and expenditure, which doesn't correlate with the act of laughing. It would not make sense to laugh for no 'account'.

questions.question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

A young girl was kidnapped from the __**mainly street in**__ 3 o’clock yesterday afternoon.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 4'** i.e. **'Main street at'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Main street"** is correct because it refers to the principal street of a town, which is usually in a central location.
 
• The preposition** "at"** is used to denote a specific time on the clock.
 
• When** referring to a specific time** during the day, **"at"** is the appropriate preposition to use.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* 'A young girl was kidnapped from the **main street at** 3 o’clock yesterday afternoon.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Let's briefly look at the other options:
 
 
• **"Main streets in" **- This option is incorrect because "main streets" would suggest multiple principal streets which is typically not the case for most towns or cities. Additionally, "in" is not the correct preposition to use with a specific time.
 
• **"Main street on"** - This is incorrect because "on" is not the appropriate preposition to use with a specific time. "On" is usually used with dates or days of the week.

questions.question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.

P. gangrene, who had recovered from Covid-19 infection and

Q. gallstones resulting in gangrene of gallbladder requiring urgent surgery

R. presented with severe inflammation of gallbladder without

S. we recently successfully treated five patients for gallbladder
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'** i.e.** 'SPRQ'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **S. **"We recently successfully treated five patients for gallbladder" - This is the** introductory clause** that sets up the subject of the sentence.
 
• **P.** "gangrene, who had recovered from Covid-19 infection and" - This** clause provides additional information** about the patients, explaining that they had gallbladder gangrene and had recovered from Covid-19.
 
• **R.** "presented with severe inflammation of gallbladder without" - This clause** continues to describe** the patients' medical condition.
 
• **Q. **"gallstones resulting in gangrene of gallbladder requiring urgent surgery" - This **clause concludes the sentence **by explaining the result of the patients' condition and what was required.

Therefore, the **correct answer** is:** 'SPRQ'.**
